argument: When several models explain the same observations, a model that compresses the data and its own specification more effectively often captures more reusable structure. In MDL form, selection minimizes a total code length such as $L(M)+L(D\mid M)$ rather than fit alone.
boundary: Compression depends on the representation language and coding scheme.
The shortest model can be scientifically wrong when the hypothesis class omits the true mechanism.
MDL is a model-selection principle, not a guarantee of causal interpretation.
